fields.v: N/A as configurations: no configuration is run; the study evaluates a metric (token spend) over natural use of two anonymised agents. No success criterion for the agents stated by the authors; quality and cost verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors. Values: within-person elasticity d = 0.26 [0.19, 0.32] (IV 0.48); commits on tokens 0.13 [0.03, 0.32]; between-person slope 0.38; work metrics explain 38% between and 13% within; spend not tied to output 3.0% floor to ~39-42% upper bound; by dominant tool share 43% (Agent A only), 37% (Agent B only), 34% (both); within-person slope 0.20 on Agent A-dominant weeks vs 0.49 on Agent B-dominant weeks

fields.v: Spend varies mostly between engineers (person explains 79% of deviance in sample); doubling an engineer's commits goes with ~20% more tokens, doubling spend with ~10% more commits; within commit quintiles the 90th percentile spend is 39-240x the 10th; up to about two fifths of spend not tied to the week's commits; role and team predict held-out engineers worse than the weekly average (-6%). Survey: 89% of technical evaluations report non-coding use; hours saved rise with non-coding breadth (0.24 [0.06, 0.43]) but not with coding use (0.08 [-0.10, 0.27])

fields.v: Associations not causal effects (engineers choose spend); one company that builds AI coding tools (some use may be testing its own agents), established codebases, voluntary use; commits miss quality, review and design work; five weeks only; telemetry lacks session content, so spend not tied to output cannot be split into useful work and waste; self-reported hours may be overstated. Gaps: record which task each agent session served; develop validated measures of the value of agent-assisted work

fields.v: No reporting inconsistency found: 'of the 34 engineers in the top decile by tokens per commit in odd weeks, only 17 remain there in even weeks' (p. 10, SM A) agrees with Fig. 12 (17 in the top decile of both halves, 34 in the top decile of only one half = 17 odd-only + 17 even-only; overlap 50%). Agents and models anonymised. Raw data and survey not published (anonymized records possibly under NDA via the JetBrains authors); replication package with analysis scripts and supplementary material: github.com/CMUSTRUDEL/token-study-replication. No pre-registration. Programming language: Not stated
